inferences: Positioning in one line: Essos sells certainty, not surgery. Every page leads with vetting (30+ US board-certified surgeons, named, with institution logos) and with removal of friction (one concierge, one price, one place). The brand is a guide/guarantor, not a clinic, so imagery should never look like a clinic ad.

Tone of voice is calm, declarative, second-person and slightly wry ("nothing gets lost in translation — literally", "Cheap isn't the red flag. Unvetted is.", "shouldn't feel like a second job"). Headlines are short serif statements; body is plain sans. Organic posts reframe fear into a checklist question ("Have I compared my options?"). This is editorial, not promotional.

Two visual registers coexist on-brand. (1) Site + paid-looking posts (E1, E2, C1, hero-poster): light, airy, warm, film-grain, no vignette, dark text on pale sky or a plain warm seamless. (2) Organic IG (A-tier, F1): near-black, one light, heavy corner fall-off, white serif. The guide posts (E3-E6) sit between: a naturally lit photo with a gradient added only where text sits. The user's current feedback (less severe vignette, more hopeful, remove tint on plain-colour people) is a move from register 2 toward the middle register, which is where E3/E5 already live; treat E3/E5 as the target, not A1.

The three site hero photos show Essos's own definition of a person-picture: full-length or profile, seamless warm-neutral backdrop (taupe, caramel), diffused soft light, low contrast, visible grain, no props, no expression beyond stillness, eyes closed or looking away. Our original 8 AI people match this brief except the backdrop is much darker; the user's 'go back to the original' is consistent with the site.

The 'purple undertone' in E4 is measurably a red/magenta-leaning shadow (hue ~13) against peach highlights, with green suppressed relative to both red and blue; it is not a blue-violet cast. Recipe: split-tone shadows toward mauve/plum (approx #4A2A33 to #5A3540 in the deepest values), keep midtones warm, keep highlights peach/ivory; in prompt language 'shadows fall into a soft mauve-plum, not brown or black; highlights stay warm peach'. Applied to backgrounds: a dusty-rose or charcoal wall whose shadow side drifts toward plum. Keep it at low saturation so it reads as film (Portra/Cinestill) rather than a colour grade.

Why pass-10 scenes read as AI although they are 'hyper-real': everything is golden-hour, every object is perfectly placed and centred, every surface is clean, every image has the same tonal curve and the same 50mm-f/1.8 shallow depth, skies are always sunset, no negative space is 'wasted', and the vignette is symmetrical. Real editorial travel photography has boring light (overcast, midday shade, mixed tungsten), off-centre framing, cropped objects at the edge, dust, creases, one slightly wrong thing. The pass-7 hotel bed the user liked was bright, daylight, wide, slightly cluttered (tray, flowers, chair, curtain) and had a real window view; it looked like a hotel's own photo.

Methods to de-AI the still lifes (rank order I would test): (a) light change: overcast or north-window daylight instead of golden hour; (b) camera change: 28-35mm, f/5.6, more in focus, slight tilt, subject off-centre or cut by the frame; (c) imperfection: creased linen, a used glass, a charger cable, fingerprints on glass, a slightly crooked lamp; (d) grain and halation via prompt ('Portra 400 pushed one stop, soft halation on highlights'); (e) do the darkening in PIL afterwards (radial mask, 18-23% weaker than pass 10) rather than in the prompt, so the model stops re-rendering the whole scene darker and more polished; (f) crop from a wider generation so composition is not model-centred; (g) fewer 'hero' objects: one cup, not a styled tray.

'18-23% less severe' vignette: pass-10 corners are roughly 8-12 luma (near black). Target corners around 20-28 luma with the fall-off starting further out (radius ~0.65 of the half-diagonal instead of ~0.5), and lift the black point slightly so shadows keep colour (this is also where the mauve undertone lives). 'More hopeful' is best done with a warmer, slightly brighter key and an open window/sky somewhere in frame rather than by lifting the whole exposure.

For people on plain colour walls the user wants two variants: (A) no tint at all, the wall rendered flat at the palette hex with only natural light fall-off; (B) 10-15% of A-tier intensity, i.e. corners only ~10-15% darker than the wall, invisible until you look. Both should keep the original-8 lighting (one soft warm side key, matte skin, Portra) and drop the pass-8/10 'darkened softly vignetted edges' sentence entirely.

The dim text-backdrop set (F1) is a different product from the still lifes: it is a slide background, so it needs low contrast, no bright focal point, a large empty area for centred text, and a global dim of roughly 55-65% (F1 shadows sit at 28-43 luma with sat 0.2-0.27, i.e. lifted, low-saturation, slightly warm). Subjects should be recognisable but unimportant: palms at dusk, a room with sheer curtains, a hotel corridor, a plane window, the Bosphorus from a taxi, a bedside lamp, a linen close-up. Blurs: generate the same scenes then Gaussian-blur 8-20 px and dim in PIL, or prompt 'out of focus, seen through a rain-streaked window' for optical-looking softness. Purple variants: mauve-plum shadows with a faint warm highlight, kept under sat 0.3 so white text still reads as neutral.

Compliance and trust: AI people must not be captioned as patients (the site's real patient story uses a real photo and a first name). Named real surgeons and institution logos are the site's trust engine; organic content can reference 'a medical board of 30+ U.S. surgeons' as text but should not fabricate doctor imagery, clinic interiors with signage, or before/after results. Turkey imagery should be cultural-neutral (tea glass, Bosphorus, cobbles, hotel) and never show operating rooms or bandages.

Typography for any overlaid text: PSTimes-like high-contrast serif for headlines (Times-family fallback), a neutral grotesk (ABC Repro-like) for body and labels, cream #EBE4D1 or page cream #F5F1E5 text on dark, near-black #171715 text on light. Gold #C9A84C exists only as a micro-accent.
web.brief:
ESSOS RESEARCH + DESIGN BRIEF (for the pass-11 image set)

1. Who Essos is, in its own words (essos.com, App Store, IG)
Essos, "Essos Technologies Incorporated", New York, is a platform to "Book Safe Medical Procedures Worldwide". It "is the trusted way to access world-class elective procedures safely and affordably" and its mission is "to make world-class healthcare accessible to everyone, everywhere." The thesis is that patients already go abroad ("over 2 million Americans" a year) "but they're doing it the hard way"; Essos is "your trusted guide". Three principles from /about: "Verified, Not Listed", "No Middlemen", "Always On Your Side". The product is a concierge plus a vetted network: "Every clinic on Essos is reviewed by our Medical Board of 30+ board-certified surgeons, led by our Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Erez Dayan (formerly Chief Resident in Plastic Surgery at Massachusetts General Hospital/Harvard Medical School)." 21 board members are named with headshots and cities (Rohrich, Salinas, Chang, Molina, Azouz...), and logos of Harvard Medical School, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, University of Toronto and NYU Langone sit on every page. Money claims: "up to 80% less than the same treatments in the U.S.", rhinoplasty "up to $20,000 in savings", all-inclusive from $3,000-3,200. The site is bigger than the IG positioning (8 treatment categories, 15+ countries, Mexico as a second hub), but the Instagram and guide posts concentrate on rhinoplasty and hair transplants in Turkey, which is what this image set serves.

2. Customer journey (site): Intake, "complete a short form" (the "2-minute questionnaire" on IG) -> Explore treatment options -> Match with a certified clinic -> Book your procedure and trip. Service layer: Consultation with a care advisor -> Travel logistics "outbound and return, fully coordinated" -> Personal concierge "from booking through recovery" -> Financing "no brokers or hidden fees". The patient story shows the lived version: a texted human ("a real person, not a chatbot") who answers in minutes; a driver with a name sign; hotel paperwork ready; the driver waiting during surgery; coffee with another patient in recovery. These are the moments organic stills should depict: the phone on the nightstand, the car at arrivals, the hotel bed, the tea, the window, the quiet morning after. Never the operating room.

3. How Essos builds trust (site mechanics, to mirror visually)
- Named, credentialed people (board headshots, institution logos rendered in neutral black so no logo shouts).
- Transparency language: "Crystal clear", "no hidden charges, no surprise bills", "We do the vetting. You make the decision."
- Editorial standards page: every clinical article is medically reviewed, AI-assisted content disclosed, corrections policy. The brand is comfortable admitting AI helps, which supports using AI imagery as long as it never poses as a real patient.
- Honesty as a feature: the patient story praises a surgeon who was "openly, unflinchingly honest" and said no to something.
- Reframing fear: "Cheap isn't the red flag. Unvetted is." Guide posts are questions a careful person asks ("Have I compared my options?", "Does my surgeon know my full medical history?", "Are we picturing the same result?").

4. Tone of voice: calm, second-person, declarative, occasionally wry. Short serif headline, plain sans body. No exclamation marks, no "transform your look", no urgency, no glamour. The word that recurs is "safe"; the emotional promise is "so you never have to second-guess your choice."

5. Visual language, measured
- Type: PSTimes (high-contrast serif) for headers, ABC Repro (grotesk) for body. IG uses the same pair.
- Colour: site is cream #F5F1E5 / pearl #EBE4D1 on near-black #171715, taupes #D8D4CA / #BCB6A7 / #8D897D, gold micro-accent #C9A84C. No purple, rose or peach in the site CSS; those come from the IG palette only.
- Photography on the site: three images, all one person on a plain warm-neutral seamless (taupe, caramel), soft diffused light, low contrast, real grain, no props, stillness (eyes closed, profile, head back). This is the closest published cousin of our original 8 AI people; the only difference is backdrop darkness.
- Site/paid posts E1, E2, C1: light, airy, warm, film grain, no vignette, dark text on pale sky. Guide posts E3-E6: naturally lit portrait, gradient only where text needs it. Organic A-tier and F1: near-black, one light, heavy corner fall-off, white serif, the wordmark small.
- Measured shadows: E4 (the purple reference) has shadows at hue ~13, sat 0.55 (red-mauve), while our AI posts E3/E5 sit at hue 29-34 (brown). The "purple undertone" is therefore a magenta/plum shift of the shadows with green suppressed, under warm peach highlights, not a blue cast. F1 backdrops sit at 28-43 luma, sat 0.20-0.27: dim, lifted, low-saturation, slightly warm. The original 8 people have near-neutral blacks (sat 0.08).

6. What each set must do (design + marketing intent)
A. People (up to ~24): go back to the original-8 look and E3/E5. One soft warm side key, matte skin with pores, Portra grain, profile or three-quarter, eyes closed or gaze off-frame, cream/black/brown knitwear, no jewellery beyond a stud. Backgrounds one palette colour per person; variant 1 = flat wall, zero corner tint; variant 2 = 10-15% corner darkening only. "More hopeful" = a warmer key, a slightly lifted black point, a hint of open air (window light quality) and a relaxed, not solemn, mouth. Keep the six new pass-10 faces; vary age/hair against the existing pool. Never caption them as patients.
B. Still lifes / scenes (up to ~18): pass-10 darkening minus ~20% (corners around 20-28 luma, fall-off starting further out, black point lifted so shadows hold colour). To stop them looking AI: overcast or north-window daylight instead of golden hour; 28-35mm, deeper focus, off-centre or edge-cropped subjects; one imperfect detail (creased sheet, used glass, cable, fingerprints); do the darkening in PIL on a brighter, wider generation instead of asking the model for it; fewer styled objects. Target the pass-7 hotel bed: daylight, wide, slightly cluttered, real window.
C. Purple-undertone experiments (~8-10, split between people and scenes): shadows to mauve/plum (#4A2A33-#5A3540 region), midtones warm, highlights peach/ivory, saturation kept low; try on dusty rose, charcoal and warm-brown walls and on one hotel and one dusk scene.
D. Dim text-backdrop set (separate PDF, ~16-20): F1-style slide backgrounds. Recognisable but unimportant subjects (LA palms at dusk, sheer curtains, hotel corridor, plane window, Bosphorus from a car, bedside lamp, linen close-up), globally dimmed to 25-45 luma with a large empty centre for white serif text; a second series blurred optically (8-20 px or "seen through rain-streaked glass") and a third with the plum shadow undertone. Test that cream #EBE4D1 text at 16 px stays legible on every one.

7. What organic content must convey for a new high-trust company
Competence without performance: the frame is quiet because the work is done. Real-world texture (grain, creases, ordinary light) signals honesty; perfection signals a render. Humans look like people who have been listened to, not models who have been sold to. Turkey is shown as a calm, civilised place (tea, water, stone, morning light), never as a bargain. Every image should be able to carry a checklist question or a concierge sentence in PSTimes without the picture competing.

8. Visual mistakes that would undermine trust
Symmetric heavy vignettes on faces (reads as a thriller poster, not care); golden-hour everything; centred, styled, spotless still lifes; plastic skin, rim-light halos, cut-out edges, film-frame borders; clinic interiors, scrubs, bandages, before/afters, signage or plate text that can be checked and found fake; AI faces captioned as patients or beside real surgeon names; warm white #F2DCD5 as a background; loud peach/rose walls without deepening; a visible logo larger than the caption; any purple that reads as a filter rather than film; text backdrops with a bright focal point behind the headline.

## What each tier actually looks like (measured on the post area of each screenshot; luminance 0-255)

**Tier A (organic Essos, ground truth for scenes).** Two sub-families.
- A1/A5/A6 (pool at dusk, wet skin, fabric): low-key, mean L 37-58, p50 25-56, deepest 5% at 4-7% grey. One warm light from one side; falloff toward the opposite corners is 1.9-2.4 stops to the darkest corner, 0.7-1.75 stops averaged over all four. The darkening is a broad, asymmetric gradient (A1 right edge 45 vs left 27; A6 top 52 vs bottom 23), anchored to where the light is, not a symmetric lens circle. Colour: warm amber mids/highlights (h25-35, sat 0.2-0.35), near-neutral shadows with a faint cool-magenta black (A1 deepest 20% = (16,13,14), A8 Lab hue 10). Soft focus and mild haze; medium grain; nothing above p95 ~70-115.
- A2/A3 (water, smoke): near-neutral cool grey-green, mean (27,31,33) / (22,24,23), p50 14-24, a 1-1.85 stop soft centre glow rather than a corner vignette; heavy softness. These are the "black blur from the corners" the user means.
- A4/A7/A8/A9 (skin macros, July 2025): brighter (mean L 60-93), taupe wall ~(100,87,77), almost no vignette; darkness only where skin turns away from the light. Skin: real pores, shine, matte-to-specular, warm (Lab hue 53-64).

**Tier B (realism only).** B1: macro pore grid, vellus hair, unretouched shine, minor redness. B2: 35mm candid, mean L 108, window halation, green-tinted grain in shadows, subject slightly soft, everyday clutter. What reads as real: imperfections, softness, blown windows, limited dynamic range, colour bleed.

**Tier C (Essos designed).** C1 MY-3 hotel: mid-key (p50 110), warm, blown window (184,172,152), matte soft; a good scene tonality target. C2 MA4 light grey ~(101,95,96) with slightly violet shadows; C4 MA5 navy shadows (41,45,55); C5 MA3 green (57,56,47) with warm skin. Backgrounds are flat and un-vignetted; a dark text gradient sits over the lower third.

**Tier D (external).** Note: D3/D4/D5 are labelled "AI content" by prompts.soul and D1/D2 are from the same prompt-selling carousel, so the whole D tier is AI, not real. Useful only for the idea: grey-green wall (Lab hue ~100), warm tangerine light on skin (hue 74, chroma 31), 1.3-stop falloff from lit subject to unlit wall.

**Tier E (Essos site/guide, ground truth for people).**
- E1 (real-looking man, sky): mean L 132, p50 161, highlights 195 neutral, no corner darkening; hazy overcast sky, soft frontal-top light, warm skin, chin lifted, eyes closed.
- E2 (woman, wheat): mean L 143, centre 190; strongly amber shadows (74,52,29), warm highlights (215,198,187); golden-hour side/back light with haze; no vignette (only the wheat is darker at the bottom).
- E3 (platinum woman, brown wall; AI): wall ~(117,91,67) at centre 119 falling to 47-99 at the corners, about 0.7 stops, brightest upper-left where the light comes from; skin matte with fine texture; highlights neutral, shadows warm.
- E5 (East Asian man; AI): wall olive-khaki grey (Lab a+2 b+11), window light from upper-left 150 falling to 54 at the bottom corners; face 60-70% L; hand in frame; slight softness.
- E4 (eye close-up, REAL): the purple reference (numbers below).
- E6 (Black woman, terrazzo, REAL): overcast top light, right side of the face 1-1.5 stops darker, cool-neutral highlights (Lab hue 117 C2), warm shadows (hue 48-54); pores, moles, vellus hair; slight softness.

**Tier F (dim text backdrops).** LA palms: mean L 43, p50 41, p95 75, 83% of pixels under Lab L20, corners only 0.5 stops below centre, chroma 4 (neutral-warm). Curtain room: p50 19, p95 74, deepest (10,8,6), the sheer curtain peaks at ~(92,89,85), chroma 2-3 (neutral). Global dim, slight softness, near-neutral colour.

**Originals (8 AI people).** Backdrop 4-11% grey (warm brown-black in #1, cool blue-black Lab hue 220 C3 in #2/#4); face p95 100-190; one warm key from upper front-left of the subject, 2.2-2.8 stops subject-to-backdrop; skin Portra amber (Lab hue 57-64, chroma 19-35); profile or three-quarter; no vignette needed because the backdrop is simply unlit.

## Real vs AI, and what separates them
Real: E4, E6, B1, B2 (and the organic A-tier macros A4/A7/A8/A9 read as real footage). AI: E3, E5, originals, all prior passes, and D1-D5 (labelled AI). Visible separators: real skin has an irregular pore grid, vellus hair, moles, patchy redness and pigment, asymmetric specular shine, and slight focus/motion softness; real frames have limited dynamic range (windows blow out: B2, C1), visible grain that lives in the shadows, halation, colour bleed, and untidy composition (cut-off objects, clutter). The AI frames have too-even skin, every strand of hair tidy, physically perfect single-source shading, symmetric centred framing, full-range HDR exposure with every plane sharp, clean edge separation between subject and wall, and golden-hour saturation everywhere.

## (a) PEOPLE target = E1, E2, E3, E5 + originals
- Exposure: mid-key on the face. Face and hair sit at 55-75% luminance (p50 of E1/E2 = 161/166; E3/E5 faces ~120-170). Not low-key: the originals are only dark because the backdrop is unlit; the subject itself is bright.
- Light: one soft directional key from above and slightly in front of the face (upper-left in E3/E5 and most originals), window or open-sky quality, warm (amber, Lab hue ~60). Falloff is gentle, 1/2 to 1 stop across the face, shadow side still readable. Optional faint warm rim on hair from the same side. No second light, no rim from behind.
- Contrast curve: soft film curve, lifted blacks on the person (deepest skin shadows ~ 30-40/255, never crushed), highlights rolled off (p95 ~170-200), no clipped skin.
- Vignette: none. E1/E2 have zero corner darkening; E3/E5 show only the natural 0.5-0.7 stop falloff of the single light across the wall, brighter where the light enters, darker on the far side, never all four corners.
- Background: plain matte wall in the chosen palette colour, rendered at its true value (E3 brown ~(117,91,67); MA4 grey ~(101,95,96); MA5 navy ~(43,48,64)). One side of the wall may be 1/2 stop brighter from the key. For the originals-style option: unlit warm charcoal backdrop, 5-10% grey, subject 2-2.5 stops brighter than it.
- Colour: warm amber skin (Portra-like), neutral highlights, shadows warm (not purple unless option c). Saturation muted, chroma ~15-30 on skin, near zero on highlights.
- Grain: fine organic 35mm/Portra 400 grain, visible mainly in midtones and shadows.
- Focus: eyes sharp, ears/back of hair slightly soft, wall soft (85mm f/2 feel).
- Skin: real pores, fine facial hair, slight unevenness and natural shine; no airbrushing.
- Crop: profile or three-quarter head-and-shoulders, subject off-centre facing into the empty side; full-length only for the window man.
- "Hopeful" here means: chin lifted or gaze raised toward the light, eyes closed or soft gaze, relaxed mouth or faint smile, light arriving from above-front so the face is lit rather than emerging from darkness, and an open, un-dark background. Prompt words: "lifted chin, calm face turned toward a soft daylight from above; the light reaches the whole face; open, quiet background at its true colour; no darkened corners or vignette".
- Tint options: (i) none; (ii) 10-15% of Essos: "a barely perceptible natural lens falloff, corners about 15-20% darker than the centre, no visible edge darkening, no blur". Never the pass 8/10 circular vignette on people.

## (b) SCENE vignette = tier A
- Strength: centre to darkest corner 1.9-2.4 stops (A1 2.4, A6 2.3, A5 1.9); averaged over all four corners 0.7-1.75 stops because it is asymmetric. Corners land at 4-7% grey, effectively black with a hint of colour; centre around 25-40% grey (mean L 37-58, p50 25-56). Highlights peak only at ~40-45% (p95 ~70-115), so the whole frame is already 1.5-2 stops under a normal exposure before the corners fall away.
- Shape: not a symmetric lens circle. It is a broad soft gradient anchored to a single light (pool light, one lamp): the side and corner nearest the light stay 1 stop brighter than the opposite side (A1 right 45 vs left 27; A6 top 52 vs bottom 23). Radius is large: the darkening begins about a third of the way from the centre and reaches black only in the last 10-15% of the frame.
- Blur: yes, the darkened areas are also softer (A2 water, A3 smoke are entirely soft; A1's pool edges melt). Think "shadows are out of focus and slightly hazy", not sharp-black.
- Colour: warm amber in what is lit (h25-35), shadows near-neutral with a faint cool-magenta black; overall low saturation (0.2-0.35).
- The 20% less severe version (target ~1.6-1.9 stops to the darkest corner, corners ~8-10% grey, centre ~35-45%): "one soft warm light on the subject; the surroundings fall away gently into deep shadow, darkest in the far corners, still showing shape and texture in the shadows; corners very dark but not black; the darkening starts well away from the centre and is heavier on the side away from the light; shadows are slightly soft and hazy". Add hopefulness by lifting the overall key half a stop (p50 ~50-70) and letting one highlight be daylight-white rather than amber.
- The 10-15% version (0.2-0.35 stops): "even, natural exposure with only the faint corner falloff of a fast prime lens; corners about 15-20% darker than the centre; no visible darkened edges, no blur in the corners".

## Fixing the "too hyper-real, looks AI" scenes (the pass-7 hotel bed is the model)
1. One light source only: window daylight or a single lamp; ban golden-hour sunsets and multiple practicals.
2. Limited dynamic range: let the window blow out to white (C1, B2), do not recover highlights; shadows fall to soft black.
3. Shallow depth of field and a single plane of focus; something in the foreground out of focus; slight overall softness, no oversharpening.
4. Off-centre, partial, cut-off framing: edge of a bed, corner of a chair, curtain half in frame; never the full room laid out.
5. Lived-in imperfection: creased linen, a glass with a water ring, dust in the light, worn stone; ban showroom-new surfaces.
6. Muted film colour with grain and slight halation; hazy overcast or soft north-window light rather than orange sun.
7. Use the pass-7 hotel image as an image reference for re-edits so the model anchors to that tonality.
8. Keep hard rules: no text, logos, signage, badges, plates; no borders.

## (c) PURPLE UNDERTONE = E4 (and E6)
- Split-tone in E4: skin midtones and highlights stay warm amber (Lab hue 50-60, chroma 22-27 on the mids, chroma ~3 neutral at the top). Only the deepest tones (L<20, about 37% of the frame: hair, eye socket, the dark-skin shadow side) swing to a desaturated mauve-plum: Lab a+10 b+4, hue ~20, chroma ~11; in RGB the shadow average is (34,19,24), blue above green under a red lead. It is a plum-black, not blue or violet. The dark-skin half shows it most: shadows go from amber (hue 47) to mauve (hue 21) as they deepen. No purple in the highlights, so the picture never looks filtered.
- E6 shows the darkened treatment (right half of the face 1-1.5 stops down) but its numbers are warm in the shadows and cool-neutral in the highlights (hue 117, chroma 2). Visually the shaded cheek reads slightly plum because cool skylight meets brown skin; that is the natural version of the same effect. The organic A1/A8 blacks also carry it (RGB blue > green).
- Three prompt phrasings, increasing strength:
  1. Subtle: "Natural warm skin; the deepest shadows and blacks carry a faint cool mauve tint, like overcast skylight in the shade; midtones and highlights stay warm and neutral."
  2. Medium (E4 match): "Warm amber skin in the light; shadows and hair fall into a muted plum-mauve black, a soft purple undertone in the darkest tones only; highlights clean and neutral; low saturation overall."
  3. Strong: "Split-toned: warm amber highlights and midtones against dusty plum-violet shadows; the shadow side of the face and the background darkness are tinted mauve; still muted, filmic, no magenta cast on the skin's lit side."
- For still-life backgrounds use phrasing 1 or 2 on the shadow areas of the wall, water or fabric: "shadows tinted dusty plum, lit areas warm".

## (d) DIM TEXT-BACKDROP = F1 + A1..A4 (separate PDF)
- Dimming: the whole frame is pulled down about 2-2.5 stops uniformly: p50 at 19-41 (7-16% grey), p95 at ~75 (30% grey), deepest tones 6-14. Only the brightest object (sheer curtain, dusk sky) reaches ~35%. Nothing white survives, so white serif copy is the brightest thing on the card by a wide margin.
- Vignette: almost none on top of the dim (0.5 stops in the palms, and in the room the darkness is on the side away from the window). A1-A4 add the soft centre-glow/dark-corner gradient described in (b); combining "F1 dim" with a mild (b) gradient gives the target.
- Softness: gentle overall soft focus, as if slightly out of focus or seen through haze; edges of palms and curtain folds are readable but never crisp; A2/A3 water and smoke are fully soft and abstract.
- What survives: silhouettes and large shapes (palm trunks against sky, curtain folds, radiator slats, suitcase edge, horizon line, city glow), a few small highlight accents (curtain, sky band), low-contrast texture. Small detail and anything busy is gone. Content is calm and generic: LA dusk skyline, dim hotel room, sheer curtain and window, water, smoke, wall-and-light; the F1 set has empty middle areas where the copy sits.
- Colour: near-neutral warm (Lab chroma 2-4, hue 55-85): a muted brown-grey. Not orange, not blue. For the purple variants, use phrasing (c)1-2 on the shadows: plum-tinted blacks, warm-neutral highlights.
- Why it works behind white serif text: p95 of the background sits below 30% grey, so the 90%+ white type has 6+ stops of contrast everywhere; low local contrast and softness mean no edges compete with letterforms; the neutral cast keeps the type from looking coloured; a faint light in one region (curtain, sky) gives the card depth without fighting the copy.
- Prompt skeleton for the set: "{scene}, seen in very low light: the whole picture dim and quiet, about two stops underexposed, soft focus and slight haze, only broad shapes and one faint light (a sheer curtain, a dusk sky) remaining; muted near-neutral brown-grey tones, {optional: shadows tinted dusty plum}; calm, empty centre; real photograph, fine grain; no text, no logos, no signage, no borders."

## Image-count sketch (~80)
People ~40: 14 people (8 originals + 6 pass-10 new) in E-style mid-key, no vignette, plus 8-10 variants at 10-15% falloff and 6-8 with purple-shadow option. Scenes ~24: 6 pass-7 style daylight scenes re-edited with the 20%-softer A gradient, 6 purple-shadow variants, plus hotel/airport/Istanbul from the pass-7 hotel-bed tonality. Dim backdrops ~16 (separate PDF): 8 F1-style neutral, 8 with plum shadows.

inferences: The strongest single cause of the 'AI' read in the pass-10 scenes is prompt contamination: the human realism block ('visible pores, fine facial hair, flyaway hairs, warm light on skin') was pasted into no-people scenes, so the model over-resolved every surface with skin-grade micro-texture and warmed everything as if lighting a face. This is inferred from the JSON prompts plus the look of the images; not tested in isolation.

The pass-7 suite reads real largely because it is compositionally and tonally a near-copy of C1 (a real photo) and was generated before the mood block existed: mid-key window daylight, slight haze, low global contrast, no vignette. The exact pass-7 scene prompt is lost, so this is reconstructed from the people prompt of that pass and the image itself.

The heavy vignette fails on people because tier E and the originals both keep the background tonally flat and let the DESIGN layer (a text band or gradient) do the darkening; a baked-in photographic vignette then double-darkens once the designer overlays copy, and it reads as an 'effect' rather than a lit wall.

gpt-image-class models take mood adjectives as objects to render: 'darkened corners' becomes a literal radial vignette, 'one soft directional light' becomes a single dramatic spotlight, 'golden hour/sunset' becomes a saturated orange sun in frame, 'film' becomes a border, 'real skin texture' becomes crisp micro-detail everywhere. Fewer adjectives should produce fewer rendered effects.

A 10-15% 'Essos intensity' on people should be expressed to the model as 'barely perceptible' falloff or, better, not asked of the model at all and applied in PIL afterward, since the model cannot dose an effect as a percentage (see the pass-3 S-curve failure in the log).
Purple undertone should be described as shadow colour ('shadows lean mauve/violet-brown, highlights stay peach'), not as a purple light source, otherwise the model will add a purple lamp or gel.
diag.brief:
DIAGNOSIS OF PASSES 7, 8 AND 10 (evidence: the contact sheets, the stored pass-10 prompts, tiers A/C/E/F)

Summary. Pass 7 scenes read real because they were mid-key, soft, low-contrast daylight frames that closely mirror C1 (a real hotel photo) and carried no mood block. Pass 8 and 10 scenes read AI because (a) the people realism block was pasted verbatim into no-people scene prompts, (b) the mood block asks for four literal effects at once (vignette, single dramatic light, warm light, film grain) which the model renders as a stack of post-processing, and (c) every scene brief lists 3-4 hero props with a sunset/golden-hour/night time, which the model stages as a product shot. On people, the baked-in vignette contradicts tier E and the originals, both of which keep the wall flat and let the design layer do any darkening.

1. CONCRETE TELLS THAT MAKE THE PASS-10 SCENES READ AS AI (from the last 6 of the pass-10 sheet, plus the armchair close crop)
- Prop-list staging: each prompt names exactly its hero props and they all appear, centred and unobstructed (blanket + water bottle on the seat; scarf + passport on the tray; towels + carafe + eucalyptus; tea glass balanced on the rail). Real rooms have things that were not asked for and things half cut off.
- Everything in focus at once: in the armchair scene the picture frame, plant, chair weave, glass, towels AND the minarets through the sheer curtain are all sharp. A real 35mm frame at that light level would have one plane sharp.
- Uniform micro-detail: the towel loops, the linen weave, the eucalyptus leaves and the rug fibres all carry the same crisp texture density; that is the 'visible pores, flyaway hairs' instruction applied to fabric and stone.
- Perfect surfaces: no scuffs, no water rings, no fingerprints on glass, no creases in the folded towels beyond the designed fold, no dust on the stone counter, no cable or outlet on any wall.
- Symmetric, art-directed placement: objects sit at pleasing thirds; the tea glass on the rail and the passport on the tray are exactly where a stylist would put them, not where a traveller would drop them.
- Impossible or over-dramatic single light: one warm spotlight-like source with everything else falling to black (entryway, car seat). Real interiors have fill from walls, ceilings and windows; the tell is that shadows go to pure black next to a lit object.
- Radial vignette as an overlay: the darkening is circular and centred on the frame, not on the light source; it darkens the window side just as much as the wall side (car seat, ferry deck), which no real lens or room does.
- Over-saturated orange sunsets: airplane and ferry both put a bright sun disc in frame with an orange-to-navy gradient; the Bosphorus horizon in C1 and in the pass-7 suite is hazy and pale.
- 'Render' depth of field: bokeh that is uniformly creamy with a hard focus plane (vanity, car seat), the CGI thin-lens look rather than optical falloff with some field curvature.
- Colour cast applied globally: the same amber applied to cream leather, white towels, clouds and stone; real white balance leaves whites nearly white.
- Extra realism cues rendered as props: 'fine organic film grain' becomes a visible uniform grain layer; in pass 7 the same wording produced a sprocket border on two frames.
- Everything is too dark to be a usable photo: the entryway is near-black, which reads as a graded render, not a room someone photographed (the log already flagged #20).

2. WHAT THE PASS-7 HOTEL SUITE DID RIGHT THAT PASS 10 LOST
- It is C1 in disguise: same bed-into-window composition, same green velvet chair, tray with flowers and water, sheer curtain, hazy Bosphorus. Copying a real photograph's composition inherits its plausibility.
- Mid-key exposure with a slightly blown window and low global contrast; whites stay white, the sky is pale and hazy, the sun is not in frame.
- One dominant soft source (window daylight) with natural room fill; shadows are grey-brown, not black.
- Some disorder: the duvet is rumpled and asymmetric, the curtain is caught mid-motion, the tray is off-centre, the lamp is cut by the frame.
- No vignette, no grain overlay, no colour cast. Pass 8's re-edit of the same image (mood_v4 row 3 col 2) shows the loss exactly: the same frame turned orange-brown with black corners and instantly looks graded.
- It was a scene brief with a place, not a prop list; the model chose the objects.

3. WHY THE HEAVY VIGNETTE ON PEOPLE READS WRONG AGAINST TIER E
- E1: man on a bright, cool overcast sea/sky gradient, mid-to-high key, dark text on the light area. No vignette at all; hope is carried by brightness.
- E3 (our AI person, the reference the user says to draw to): flat, evenly lit warm brown wall; the lower half is darkened by a DESIGN band for the copy, not by the photo. The originals_8people sheet is the same idea: near-black warm backdrop, gradual falloff from a single soft key, no corner ring.
- E5/E6: subject lit by real directional light against an evenly toned wall; darkening in E6 comes from the face's own shadow side, and text is placed there.
- Consequences: (i) the baked-in vignette double-darkens once the designer adds an overlay band or gradient; (ii) a circular vignette on a plain wall reads as a Lightroom effect because a plain wall has no depth for light to fall off into; (iii) it pushes the whole set towards moody/anxious, which contradicts 'hopeful and optimistic'; (iv) on light colours (pearl white, peach, dusty rose) the vignette muddies the brand colour so it no longer matches C2-C5. The A-tier vignette belongs to scenes-as-text-backdrops, which is a different job from a portrait.

4. FIVE-PLUS METHODS TO MAKE GENERATED STILL LIFES READ AS PHOTOGRAPHS

Method 1: Documentary imperfection (mess, wear, accident)
(i) Mechanism: the model stages what it is told; give it disorder and cut-offs so it cannot centre and clean. Real interiors are identified by the things nobody arranged.
(ii) Prompt language: 'A hotel room as a guest actually left it: the duvet pushed back, a phone charger on the nightstand, a half-drunk glass of water with a ring on the table, one slipper out of frame. Nothing is styled or centred; objects are cut off by the edge of the frame. Slight clutter, small scuffs and fingerprints are fine.'
(iii) Risk: too much mess reads cheap, against quiet luxury; the model can invent legible text on chargers or labels, so keep the 'no text, no logos' negative. Keep mess to 1-2 items.

Method 2: Specific camera, lens, film stock and technical flaws
(i) Mechanism: name a real capture chain and its faults (slight underexposure, motion softness, mixed white balance) so the model imitates a photograph rather than a render.
(ii) Prompt language: 'Shot on a Contax T2 with Kodak Portra 400, pushed one stop, handheld at 1/30s: slight motion softness, mild grain in the shadows, gentle halation on the window, a little mixed white balance between the tungsten lamp and the daylight, shadows lifted and slightly milky. No borders, sprocket holes or film-frame edges; no date stamp.'
(iii) Risk: the literal readings already logged: 'film' produces a frame, 'grain' produces a uniform noise layer, 'halation' can become a glow halo. Always keep the border and halo negatives.

Method 3: Ambient/available light, lower contrast, mid-key
(i) Mechanism: the AI look comes from one dramatic key falling to black. Real rooms have bounce fill; ask for flat, soft, slightly overexposed daylight and refuse 'one light'.
(ii) Prompt language: 'Overcast late-morning daylight from a large window, bouncing off pale walls so the shadows are soft grey-brown and open, not black. Low overall contrast, whites slightly overexposed, the sky pale and hazy with no sun in frame. Muted true-to-life colour, no warm colour grade, no vignette.'
(iii) Risk: loses some of the tier-A drama and can look like a real-estate listing; recover the mood afterwards with a PIL vignette at 18-23% below pass-10 strength rather than in the prompt.

Method 4: Reference-anchored edit (use the pass-7 suite, id 687d39f6-b9d5-46aa-80ff-14b5d1861daa, or C1 as style reference)
(i) Mechanism: edits keep the reference's tonal statistics, so the model inherits the haze, contrast and exposure of a real-looking image instead of synthesising them.
(ii) Prompt language: 'Match the light, exposure, contrast, colour and softness of the reference photograph exactly: same hazy window daylight, same pale sky, same open shadows and slightly milky blacks. Change only the scene to {SCENE}. Keep it as plain and unstyled as the reference.'
(iii) Risk: composition drift towards a copy of the suite (bed and window everywhere); the model may also carry over the reference's objects. State 'different room, different objects' explicitly and vary the scene list.

Method 5: Restraint (short prompt, few adjectives)
(i) Mechanism: every adjective becomes a rendered effect; a 25-word prompt lets the model fall back on its photographic prior, which is more ordinary than anything the mood block asks for.
(ii) Prompt language: 'Photo of a hotel bathroom sink in Istanbul, morning. No people, no text.' Or: 'A quiet clinic waiting room, afternoon, window light. Unstyled. No people, no text, no logos.'
(iii) Risk: less brand consistency between images and occasional stock-photo blandness; the palette and mood then have to come from PIL grading and the designer's overlay, which is where tier A actually gets it.

Method 6: Phone-camera candid
(i) Mechanism: 'iPhone photo' pulls the model toward small-sensor rendering: deep depth of field, slight HDR flatness, no bokeh, mild noise, casual framing. This directly kills the 'render DOF' and spotlight tells.
(ii) Prompt language: 'Casual iPhone photo taken by the guest, slightly tilted, deep depth of field, mild HDR flatness, natural mixed lighting, nothing arranged. No filter, no vignette, no text.'
(iii) Risk: can look too casual for quiet luxury; best used for the dim text-backdrop set (F1) where the photo is dimmed to 25% anyway and only needs to feel real.

Method 7: Do the mood in post, not in the prompt
(i) Mechanism: the model cannot dose an effect ('18-23% less'), but PIL can. Generate flat/mid-key with methods 3-5, then apply a measured radial darkening, a slight desaturation and, for the purple experiments, a shadow tint toward mauve.
(ii) Implementation, not prompt: vignette mask strength ~0.55x of the pass-10 look for scenes, ~0.12x or zero for people; optional shadow-only hue shift toward #5A4A5E for the E4 experiments.
(iii) Risk: none to identity; the only risk is over-processing, so preview 3 before the batch.

Combine: for the main scene set run methods 3+4 (reference-anchored, flat daylight) and 1+2 (imperfection with a named film chain) as two distinct sub-sets, plus method 5 as a control; grade in post. For the F1 dim backdrops use method 6 or 5 and dim in PIL to 25-35% brightness with a slight navy-purple lift in the shadows.

5. PROMPT WORDS THE MODEL TAKES LITERALLY AND THAT HURT
- 'visible pores, fine facial hair, natural skin unevenness and shine, flyaway hairs, real fabric texture' in scene prompts: no skin exists, so it micro-details towels, stone and leather; also 'warm light on skin' warms everything. Remove entirely from scenes.
- 'darkened, softly vignetted edges and corners': rendered as a circular overlay centred on the frame. Replace with a light description ('light falls off toward the far side of the room') or do it in PIL.
- 'one soft directional light falling off gently into deep shadow': produces a spotlight with black surroundings. Say 'window light with soft fill from the walls'.
- 'golden hour', 'sunset', 'sunrise', 'at dusk', 'low sun outside': produce a saturated sun disc and orange sky. Say 'overcast', 'late morning', 'hazy', 'sun out of frame'.
- '35mm', 'film', 'documentary photograph', 'film grain': border and grain overlays (pass 7 sprockets). If a film stock is named, keep 'no borders, sprocket holes or frame edges'.
- 'soft focus falloff': becomes render-style bokeh; say 'moderate depth of field, most of the room in focus'.
- 'muted, slightly desaturated earthy tones' + 'warm light': combined they yield the uniform amber cast; say 'true-to-life white balance, whites stay white'.
- 'intimate', 'contemplative', 'quietly hopeful': harmless on people but on scenes they nudge toward the moody dark grade; drop them from scene prompts.
- 'Essos brand mood': meaningless to the model, occupies tokens; replace with concrete descriptors.
- Prop lists with counts ('a glass of water and a folded linen towel'): every item will be placed dead centre; describe the place and the time, name at most one object, and add 'nothing arranged, some things cut off by the frame'.
- 'plain wall' for people: fine, but 'real room wall' produced a kitchen (pass 7); keep 'no room, furniture or window visible'.
- For the purple work, do not write 'purple light' or 'purple tint'; write 'shadow side of the face and the wall lean mauve/violet-brown as in cool shade, highlights stay warm peach' so it becomes a shadow colour, not a lamp.

Practical notes for the parent: the pass-7 hotel-suite prompt is not stored (only the label), so the reference-anchored method must use the image id, not the text. build_pass11_requests.py already expects a spec.json with scene_methods, scene_purple, new_scenes, dim_scenes, dim_backdrop_t2i and dim_backdrop_purple and lists the original 8 people ids plus the 6 pass-10 new-people ids; the methods above map directly onto that schema.
